records.issue_text: [Critical/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 / app/views/embed/best.html.erb:24 — Imported feed/readability content is stored and cooked as raw_html, bypassing sanitization/markdown pipeline, then rendered with raw post.cooked, allowing script/event-handler markup in external feed content to become stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin inside the iframe; PollFeed feeds raw feed HTML straight in with no filtering
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: Post#cook returns `raw` unfiltered for raw_html cook_method, TopicEmbed.import sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` on external content (from RSS via PollFeed or readability via import_remote) with no sanitization, and best.html.erb renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The view is embedded in an iframe on the Discourse origin with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL. External feed HTML containing script/event-handler markup would thus be stored and executed — a real stored XSS introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — url is interpolated unescaped into HTML (#{url}), allowing a crafted embed URL (quotes, onerror=, etc.) to inject markup into the post body which is then rendered raw
records.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, url is only validated via `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and then interpolated unescaped: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. Quotes or event-handler attributes in the URL would inject markup, and the post is stored with cook_method raw_html and later rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view, so the injection executes in the browser.

records.issue_text: [Low/security] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:20 — e.data.height is used without validating it's a sane number; a compromised/malicious embedder can inject arbitrary strings into the iframe height attribute; cap/validate as a positive integer
records.rationale: The finding's threat model is contradicted by the diff: postMessageReceived guards with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, so only messages originating from the Discourse forum's own domain are processed. A 'malicious embedder' (the third-party site embedding the iframe) cannot send the discourse-resize message and thus cannot influence e.data.height; only the trusted Discourse origin can. Assigning an unvalidated string to iframe.height from the trusted origin is not a security defect, leaving this a vague validation preference.
